The first law states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion unless acted on by a net external force.
This is also called the law of inertia.
The second law relates force, mass, and acceleration with the equation F equals m times a.
Using F equals m times a, the net force required is 2000 newtons.
Momentum is another important concept, defined as mass times velocity.
There are two types of collisions we study: elastic collisions, where kinetic energy is conserved, and inelastic collisions, where it is not.
